name: Early Maya hieroglyphs at San Bartolo
description: Painted Maya hieroglyphs on an excavated masonry block from Las Pinturas at San Bartolo, an early witness to writing in the Maya lowlands.

date.label: approximately 300–200 BCE
date.basis: Date or interval stated or closely scoped by the cited source; see event caveats.

events.statement: A block at San Bartolo bears a column of ten painted glyphs, dated by the excavators to approximately 300–200 BCE from associated construction contexts and radiocarbon samples.
events.population: Maya scribal community at San Bartolo
events.caveats: Dates are inferences from associated charcoal and building sequences, not a direct measurement of the writing. The text is mostly not deciphered, and the block does not date invention of Maya writing.

evidence.supports: The archaeologists explain the stratigraphic and charcoal dating and the ten-sign inscription.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest cited dated event for this scoped record; a surviving witness or publication is not itself the invention date.

places.note: San Bartolo site in present-day Guatemala; country-level mapping does not claim the ancient polity had modern borders.

caveats: Connections to other Mesoamerican script traditions remain unsettled; no independent origin is asserted.

research.note: Second reader checked the original 2006 paper as indexed in NLM and available scholarly text; the age is inferred from context, not a direct measurement of the signs.
